─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n376\t\n377\t/// Retry wrapper for subprocess spawns that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n378\t///\n379\t/// ETXTBSY (\"Text file busy\") occurs when the kernel blocks execution of a binary\n380\t/// that has a write-mode file descriptor still open. This is a genuine race condition:\n381\t///\n382\t/// 1. A process writes a binary to disk and closes the file descriptor.\n383\t/// 2. The kernel's page cache and filesystem synchronization haven't fully completed.\n384\t/// 3. Another process immediately attempts to `exec()` the same binary.\n385\t/// 4. The kernel returns ETXTBSY (errno 26) because the file is still marked for write.\n386\t///\n387\t/// This is most common with:\n388\t/// - Freshly-extracted upgrade binaries executed immediately\n389\t/// - Test fixtures written and chmod'd immediately before use\n390\t/// - Any binary that's written to disk and executed in quick succession\n391\t///\n392\t/// The race is narrow (typically <100ms) but real. Retrying with a short backoff\n393\t/// is the correct fix — the file descriptor is already closed, we're just waiting\n394\t/// for the kernel to finish its internal bookkeeping.\n395\t///\n396\t/// # Parameters\n397\t///\n398\t/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n399\t/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n400\t/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n401\t///\n402\t/// # Returns\n403\t///\n404\t/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n405\t/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n406\t///\n407\t/// # When to use this helper\n408\t///\n409\t/// Use this wrapper whenever spawning a subprocess that may have been written to\n410\t/// disk immediately before execution:\n411\t///\n412\t/// - Freshly-installed or updated binaries\n413\t/// - Test fixtures created during test setup\n414\t/// - Any executable extracted from an archive and immediately run\n415\t///\n416\t/// Do NOT use this for long-running processes or stable system binaries — the\n417\t/// retry overhead is unnecessary and ETXTBSY is unlikely in those cases.\n418\t///\n419\t/// # Example\n420\t///\n421\t/// ```no_run\n422\t/// use std::path::Path;\n423\t/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry;\n424\t///\n425\t/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n426\t/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/binary\");\n427\t/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n428\t///     || async {\n429\t///         tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n430\t///             .arg(\"--version\")\n431\t///             .output()\n432\t///             .await\n433\t///     },\n434\t///     5,\n435\t///     20,\n436\t/// ).await?;\n437\t/// # Ok(())\n438\t/// # }\n439\t/// ```\n440\tpub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry<F, Fut, T>(\n441\t    spawn_fn: F,\n442\t    max_attempts: u32,\n443\t    backoff_ms: u64,\n444\t) -> std::io::Result<T>\n445\twhere\n446\t    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n447\t    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n448\t{\n449\t    let mut last_err = None;\n450\t    for     attempt = attempt + 1,\n456\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n457\t                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n458\t                        \"ETXTBSY retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n459\t                        attempt + 1\n460\t                    );\n461\t                }\n462\t                return Ok(output);\n463\t            }\n464\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(26) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n465\t                last_err = Some(e);\n466\t                warn!(\n467\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n468\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n469\t                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\n470\t                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n471\t Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting MAX_ATTEMPTS\"))\n482\t}\n483\t\n484\t/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` calls that handle ETXTBSY (errno Use this when you need to interact with the spawned\n488\t/// process (e.g., for timeout handling with `kill_on_drop`).\n489\t///\n490\t/// # Parameters\n491\t///\n492\t/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n493\t/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n494\t/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(spawn_fn, max_attempts, backoff_ms).await\n510\t}\n511\t\n512\t/// Retry wrapper for subprocess spawns with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n513\t///\n514\t/// This variant uses **exponential backoff** with jitter, making it more suitable for\n515\t/// high-concurrency scenarios where multiple processes might race for the same binary.\n516\t/// Exponential backoff prevents thundering herd problems that linear backoff can cause.\n517\t///\n518\t/// The backoff formula is: `base_ms * 2^attempt + random_jitter`, where:\n519\t/// - `base_ms` is the initial delay (default: 20ms)\n520\t/// - `attempt` is the current retry number (0-indexed)\n521\t/// - `random_jitter` is ±25% of the calculated delay to prevent synchronization\n522\t///\n523\t/// Example backoff sequence with base_ms=20:\n524\t/// - Attempt 1: ~20ms (15-25ms with jitter)\n525\t/// - Attempt 2: ~40ms (30-50ms with jitter)\n526\t/// - Attempt 3: ~80ms (60-100ms with jitter)\n527\t/// - Attempt 4: ~160ms (120-200ms with jitter)\n528\t/// - Attempt 5: ~320ms (240-400ms with jitter)\n529\t///\n530\t/// # Parameters\n531\t///\n532\t/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n533\t/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n534\t/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n535\t///\n536\t/// # Returns\n537\t///\n538\t/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n539\t/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n540\t///\n541\t/// # When to use exponential vs linear backoff\n542\t///\n543\t/// Use exponential backoff when:\n544\t/// - Spawning multiple processes concurrently that might race for the same binary\n545\t/// - Running in high-concurrency environments (CI, parallel tests)\n546\t/// - Dealing with slow filesystems where the race window might be longer\n547\t///\n548\t/// Use linear backoff (`spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry`) when:\n549\t/// - Spawning a single process in isolation\n550\t/// - The race window is known to be very short (<50ms)\n551\t/// - Minimal latency is more important than thundering herd prevention\n552\t///\n553\t/// # Example\n554\t///\n555\t/// ```no_run\n556\t/// use std::path::Path;\n557\t/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential;\n558\t///\n559\t/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n560\t/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/freshly-written-binary\");\n561\t/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential(\n562\t///     || async {\n563\t///         tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n564\t///             .arg(\"--version\")\n565\t///             .output()\n566\t///             .await\n567\t///     },\n568\t///     10,\n569\t///     20,\n570\t/// ).await?;\n571\t/// # Ok(())\n572\t/// # }\n573\t/// ```\n574\tpub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential<F, Fut, T>(\n575\t    spawn_fn: F,\n576\t    max_attempts: u32,\n577\t    base_ms: u64,\n578\t) -> std::io::Result<T>\n579\twhere\n580\t    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n581\t    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n582\t{\n583\t    use rand::Rng;\n584\t\n585\t    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n586\t    const JITTER_PERCENT: f64 = 0.25; // ±25% jitter\n587\t\n588\t    let mut last_err = None;\n589\t    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();\n590\t\n591\t    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n592\t        match spawn_fn().await {\n593\t            Ok(output) => {\n594\t                if attempt > 0 {\n595\t                    debug!(\n596\t                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n597\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n598\t                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n599\t                        \"ETXTBSY exponential retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n600\t                        attempt + 1\n601\t                    );\n602\t                }\n603\t                return Ok(output);\n604\t            }\n605\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n606\t                last_err = Some(e);\n607\t\n608\t                // Calculate exponential backoff: base_ms * 2^attempt\n609\t                let exponential_delay = base_ms * (1 << attempt);\n610\t\n611\t                // Add jitter to prevent synchronization\n612\t                let jitter_range = (exponential_delay as f64 * JITTER_PERCENT) as u64;\n613\t                let jitter = rng.gen_range(0..=jitter_range * 2);\n614\t                let delay = exponential_delay\n615\t                    .saturating_add(jitter)\n616\t                    .saturating_sub(jitter_range);\n617\t\n618\t                warn!(\n619\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n620\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n621\t                    delay_ms = delay,\n622\t                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n623\t                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in ~{}ms (exponential backoff with jitter)\",\n624\t                    attempt + 1,\n625\t                    max_attempts,\n626\t                    delay\n627\t                );\n628\t                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay)).await;\n629\t            }\n630\t            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n631\t        }\n632\t    }\n633\t\n634\t    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n635\t}\n636\t\n637\t/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n638\t///\n639\t/// Specialized version of          }\n377\t        }\n378\t    }\n379\t\n380\t    /// Validate timeout field mutual exclusivity.\n381\t    ///\n382\t    /// Legacy `timeout_secs` and new This preserves backward compatibility while allowing\n384\t    /// the new two-field timeout model.\n385\t    ///\n386\t    /// # Errors\n387\t    ///\n388\t    /// Returns an error if:\n389\t    /// self.name,\n418\t                self.timeout_secs,\n419\t                self.idle_timeout_secs,\n420\t                self.hard_timeout_secs\n421\t            );\n422\t        }\n423\t\n424\t        Ok(())\n425\t    }\n426\t}\n427\t\n428\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n429\t// Built-in adapters\n430\t//          }\n377\t        }\n378\t    }\n379\t\n380\t    /// Validate timeout field mutual exclusivity.\n381\t    ///\n382\t    /// Legacy `timeout_secs` and new This preserves backward compatibility while allowing\n384\t    /// the new two-field timeout model.\n385\t    ///\n386\t    /// # Errors\n387\t    ///\n388\t    /// Returns an error if:\n389\t    /// - `timeout_secs` is non-zero AND either `idle_timeout_secs` or `hard_timeout_secs` is non-zero\n390\t    ///\n391\t    /// # Examples\n392\t    ///\n393\t    /// ```\n394\t    /// // Valid: legacy self.name,\n418\t                self.timeout_secs,\n419\t                self.idle_timeout_secs,\n420\t                self.hard_timeout_secs\n421\t            );\n422\t        }\n423\t\n424\t        Ok(())\n425\t    }\n426\t}\n427\t\n428\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n429\t// Built-in adapters\n430\t// };\n1462\t\n1463\t            outcome\n1464\t        };\n1465\t\n1466\t        tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.agent.exit_code\", exit_code);\n1467\t\n1468\t        // Set span status: Ok for self.timeout_secs\n        } else {\n            global_timeout_secs\n        };\n        if secs == 0 {\n            Duration::ZERO\n        } else {\n            Duration::from_secs(secs)\n \"anthropic\", \"openai\", \"local\").\n    /// Defaults to \"local\" if no provider is configured.\n    pub fn gen_ai_system(&self) -> &str {\n        self.provider.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"local\")\n    }\n\n    /// Active timeout policy for this adapter.\n    ///\n    /// Distinguishes between legacy single timeout and the new two-field\n    /// (idle + hard) timeout model.\n    pub fn timeout_policy(&self) -> TimeoutPolicy {\n        let has_legacy = self.timeout_secs > 0;\n        let has_idle = self.idle_timeout_secs > 0;\n        let has_hard = self.hard_timeout_secs > 0;\n\n        if has_legacy {\n            TimeoutPolicy::Legacy\n        } else if has_idle || has_hard {\n            TimeoutPolicy::New {\n                idle_enabled: has_idle,\n                hard_enabled: has_hard,\n            }\n        } else {\n            TimeoutPolicy::Global\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Human-readable description of the active timeout policy.\n    ///\n    /// Shows which timeout mode is active and the configured values.\n    pub fn timeout_description(&self, global_timeout_secs: u64) -> String {\n        match self.timeout_policy() {\n            TimeoutPolicy::Legacy => {\n                format!(\"legacy: {}s (single timeout)\", self.timeout_secs)\n            }\n            TimeoutPolicy::New {\n                idle_enabled,\n                hard_enabled,\n            } => {\n                let mut parts = Vec::new();\n                parts.push(\"new:\".to_string());\n                if idle_enabled {\n                    parts.push(format!(\"idle={}s\", self.idle_timeout_secs));\n                }\n                if hard_enabled {\n                    parts.push(format!(\"hard={}s\", self.hard_timeout_secs));\n                }\n                if !idle_enabled && !hard_enabled {\n                    parts.push(\"both disabled\".to_string());\n                }\n                parts.join(\" \")\n            }\n            TimeoutPolicy::Global => {\n                if global_timeout_secs > 0 {\n                    format!(\"global: {}s (from config)\", global_timeout_secs)\n                } else {\n                    \"global: unlimited (0 = no timeout)\".to_string()\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Validate timeout field mutual exclusivity.\n    ///\n    /// Legacy `timeout_secs` and new `idle_timeout_secs`/`hard_timeout_secs`\n    /// cannot both be set. This preserves backward compatibility while allowing\n    /// the new two-field timeout model.\n    ///\n    /// # Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - `timeout_secs` is non-zero AND either `idle_timeout_secs` or `hard_timeout_secs` is non-zero\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// // Valid: legacy timeout alone\n    /// assert!(adapter_with_timeout_secs_only().validate_timeouts().is_ok());\n    ///\n    /// // Valid: new timeout fields together\n    /// assert!(adapter_with_new_timeouts().validate_timeouts().is_ok());\n    ///\n    /// // Valid: new timeout field alone (other set to 0)\n    /// assert!(adapter_with_idle_only().validate_timeouts().is_ok());\n    ///\n    /// // Invalid: mixing legacy and new\n    /// assert!(adapter_with_mixed_timeouts().validate_timeouts().is_err());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn validate_timeouts(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let has_legacy = self.timeout_secs > 0;\n        let has_idle = self.idle_timeout_secs > 0;\n        let has_hard = self.hard_timeout_secs > 0;\n\n        if has_legacy && (has_idle || has_hard) {\n            bail!(\n                \"adapter '{}' has incompatible timeout configuration: \\\n                 legacy field 'timeout_secs' ({}) cannot be used together with new fields \\\n                 'idle_timeout_secs' ({}) or 'hard_timeout_secs' ({}). \\\n                 Use either timeout_secs alone (legacy) or idle_timeout_secs + hard_timeout_secs (new).\",\n                self.name,\n                self.timeout_secs,\n                self.idle_timeout_secs,\n                self.hard_timeout_secs\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Built-in adapters\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Template rendering\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Substitute known variables in an invoke template.\nfn render_template(\n    template: &str,\n    workspace: &Path,\n    prompt_file: &Path,\n    bead_id: &BeadId,\n    model: &str,\n) -> String {\n    template\n        .replace(\"{workspace}\", &workspace.display().to_string())\n        .replace(\"{prompt_file}\", &prompt_file.display().to_string())\n        .replace(\"{bead_id}\", bead_id.as_ref())\n        .replace(\"{model}\", model)\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Adapter loading\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Load adapters from YAML files, with built-in defaults.\n///\n/// Built-in adapters are loaded first; user files in `dir` override by name.\npub fn load_adapters(\n    dir: &Path,\n    built_ins: &[AgentAdapter],\n) -> Result<HashMap<String, AgentAdapter>> {\n    let mut adapters = HashMap::new();\n\n    for adapter in built_ins {\n        adapters.insert(adapter.name.clone(), adapter.clone());\n    }\n\n    if dir.exists() && dir.is_dir() {\n        let entries = std::fs::read_dir(dir)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read adapters dir: {}\", dir.display()))?;\n\n        for entry in entries {\n            let entry = entry?;\n            let path = entry.path();\n            let is_yaml = path\n                .extension()\n                .is_some_and(|ext| ext == \"yaml\" || ext == \"yml\");\n            if is_yaml {\n                let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read adapter file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n                let adapter: AgentAdapter = serde_yaml::from_str(&text)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in adapter file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n                // Validate timeout field mutual exclusivity\n                adapter.validate_timeouts().with_context(|| {\n                    format!(\n                        \"adapter '{}' in file {} has invalid timeout configuration\",\n                        adapter.name,\n                        path.display()\n                    )\n                })?;\n\n                adapters.insert(adapter.name.clone(), adapter);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Log timeout policy for all loaded adapters\n    let global_timeout = 3600; // Default, will be overridden by dispatcher\n    for adapter in adapters.values() {\n        let policy = adapter.timeout_policy();\n        let desc = adapter.timeout_description(global_timeout);\n        tracing::debug!(\n            adapter = %adapter.name,\n            timeout_policy = ?policy,\n            timeout_config = %desc,\n            \"loaded adapter with timeout configuration\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    Ok(adapters)\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Dispatcher\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Executes agent processes for claimed beads.\npub struct Dispatcher {\n    adapters: HashMap<String, AgentAdapter>,\n    telemetry: Telemetry,\n    global_timeout_secs: u64,\n    /// Sanitizer applied to all trace content before writing to disk.\n    /// `None` when trace sanitization is disabled in config.\n    sanitizer: Option<Arc<Sanitizer>>,\n    /// Tsnet identity registry for per-worker network identity.\n    /// `None` when tsnet is disabled in config.\n    tsnet_registry: Option<IdentityRegistry>,\n    /// Tsnet configuration (cached from config).\n    tsnet_config: TsnetConfig,\n}\n\nimpl Dispatcher {\n    /// Create a new dispatcher, loading adapters from config.\n    pub fn new(config: &Config, telemetry: Telemetry) -> Result<Self> {\n        let adapters = load_adapters(&config.agent.adapters_dir, &builtin_adapters())?;\n        let sanitizer = build_sanitizer(config);\n        let tsnet_config = config.tsnet.clone();\n\n        // Create tsnet registry only if enabled\n        let tsnet_registry = if tsnet_config.enabled {\n            Some(IdentityRegistry::new(tsnet_config.clone()))\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        Ok(Dispatcher {\n            adapters,\n            telemetry,\n            global_timeout_secs: config.agent.timeout,\n            sanitizer,\n            tsnet_registry,\n            tsnet_config,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Create a dispatcher with explicit adapters (for testing).\n    pub fn with_adapters(\n        adapters: HashMap<String, AgentAdapter>,\n        telemetry: Telemetry,\n        global_timeout_secs: u64,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Dispatcher {\n            adapters,\n            telemetry,\n            global_timeout_secs,\n            sanitizer: None,\n            tsnet_registry: None,\n            tsnet_config: TsnetConfig::default(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Look up an adapter by name.\n    pub fn adapter(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&AgentAdapter> {\n        self.adapters.get(name)\n    }\n\n    /// List all loaded adapter names.\n    pub fn adapter_names(&self) -> Vec<&str> {\n        self.adapters.keys().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Resolve an adapter name from a model name using routing rules.\n    ///\n    /// If routing is configured in the config, returns the adapter name that\n    /// matches the model pattern (first match wins). Otherwise, returns the\n    /// default adapter name.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `model` - Model name (e.g., \"sonnet\", \"claude-opus-4-8\", \"fable\")\n    /// * `config` - Full config containing routing rules\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// The resolved adapter name (e.g., \"claude-code-glm-4.7\", \"claude-sonnet\")\n    pub fn resolve_adapter_name(&self, model: &str, config: &Config) -> String {\n        if let Some(ref routing) = config.agent.routing {\n            // Check each routing rule in order (first match wins)\n            for rule in &routing.rules {\n                match regex::Regex::new(&rule.match_model) {\n                    Ok(re) => {\n                        if re.is_match(model) {\n                            tracing::debug!(\n                                model = %model,\n                                pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                                adapter = %rule.adapter,\n                                \"routing rule matched\"\n                            );\n                            return rule.adapter.clone();\n                        }\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        // Regex was validated during config load, so this should never happen.\n                        // Fall back to default if somehow we get an invalid pattern at runtime.\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                            \"invalid routing regex pattern (should have been caught by config validation)\"\n                        );\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // No rules matched; use default_adapter if set\n            if let Some(ref default_adapter) = routing.default_adapter {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    model = %model,\n                    adapter = %default_adapter,\n                    \"no routing rules matched, using default_adapter\"\n                );\n                return default_adapter.clone();\n            }\n        }\n\n        // No routing configured or no default_adapter; fall back to agent.default\n        tracing::debug!(\n            model = %model,\n            adapter = %config.agent.default,\n            \"no routing configured, using agent.default\"\n        );\n        config.agent.default.clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Execute the agent process for a bead.\n    ///\n    /// 1. Writes the prompt to a temp file\n    /// 2. Renders the invoke template with variables\n    /// 3. Sets adapter-specific environment variables\n    /// 4. Spawns the process via `bash -c`\n    /// 5. Waits with timeout enforcement (kills on timeout, exit 124)\n    /// 6. Captures stdout, stderr, exit code\n    /// 7. Cleans up the temp file\n    #[tracing::instrument(\n        name = \"agent.dispatch\",\n        skip(self, bead_id, prompt, adapter, workspace),\n        fields(\n            needle.bead.id = %bead_id.as_ref(),\n            gen_ai.system = %adapter.gen_ai_system(),\n            gen_ai.operation.name = \"chat\",\n            gen_ai.request.id = %bead_id.as_ref(),\n            needle.agent.pid = tracing::field::Empty,\n            needle.agent.exit_code = tracing::field::Empty,\n        )\n    )]\n    pub async fn dispatch(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n        prompt: &BuiltPrompt,\n        adapter: &AgentAdapter,\n        workspace: &Path,\n    ) -> Result<ExecutionResult> {\n        // Set gen_ai.request.model if available\n        if let Some(ref model) = adapter.model {\n            tracing::Span::current().record(\"gen_ai.request.model\", model.as_str());\n        }\n\n        // Log timeout policy for this dispatch\n        let timeout_policy = adapter.timeout_policy();\n        let timeout_desc = adapter.timeout_description(self.global_timeout_secs);\n        tracing::debug!(\n            adapter = %adapter.name,\n            timeout_policy = ?timeout_policy,\n            timeout_config = %timeout_desc,\n            \"dispatching agent with timeout policy\"\n        );\n\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::DispatchStarted {\n            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n            agent: adapter.name.clone(),\n            prompt_len: prompt.content.len(),\n            template_name: prompt.template_name.clone(),\n            template_version: prompt.template_version.clone(),\n            prompt_hash: prompt.hash.clone(),\n        })?;\n\n        let result = self\n            .execute_agent(bead_id, &prompt.content, adapter, workspace)\n            .await;\n\n        // Emit completion telemetry regardless of success/failure.\n        let agent_name = adapter.name.clone();\n        let agent_model = adapter.model.clone();\n        match &result {\n            Ok(exec) => {\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.agent.pid\", exec.pid);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.agent.exit_code\", exec.exit_code);\n\n                // Extract token usage and set gen_ai.usage attributes\n                let usage = extract_tokens(&adapter.token_extraction, &exec.stdout, &exec.stderr);\n                if let Some(input_tokens) = usage.input_tokens {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"gen_ai.usage.input_tokens\", input_tokens);\n                }\n                if let Some(output_tokens) = usage.output_tokens {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"gen_ai.usage.output_tokens\", output_tokens);\n                }\n\n                // Set span status: Ok for exit_code 0, Error otherwise\n                if exec.exit_code != 0 {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\n                        \"otel.status_description\",\n                        format!(\"exit_code: {}\", exec.exit_code),\n                    );\n                }\n\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::DispatchCompleted {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                    exit_code: exec.exit_code,\n                    duration_ms: exec.elapsed.as_millis() as u64,\n                    agent: agent_name,\n                    model: agent_model,\n                });\n\n                // Emit structured timeout event if applicable.\n                if let Some(ref reason) = exec.timeout_reason {\n                    let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::AgentTimeout {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        reason: reason.clone(),\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                // Set span status on error\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", \"dispatch_error\");\n\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::DispatchCompleted {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                    exit_code: -1,\n                    duration_ms: 0,\n                    agent: agent_name,\n                    model: agent_model,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        result\n    }\n\n    /// Internal: execute the agent, ensuring temp file cleanup.\n    async fn execute_agent(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n        prompt_content: &str,\n        adapter: &AgentAdapter,\n        workspace: &Path,\n    ) -> Result<ExecutionResult> {\n        let prompt_file = write_prompt_to_temp(bead_id, prompt_content)?;\n\n        let result = self\n            .run_process(bead_id, adapter, workspace, &prompt_file)\n            .await;\n\n        // Always clean up temp file.\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&prompt_file);\n\n        result\n    }\n\n    /// Internal: spawn and manage the agent process.\n    #[tracing::instrument(\n        name = \"agent.execution\",\n        skip(self, bead_id, adapter, workspace, prompt_file),\n        fields(\n            needle.bead.id = %bead_id.as_ref(),\n            needle.agent.pid = tracing::field::Empty,\n            needle.agent.exit_code = tracing::field::Empty,\n        )\n    )]\n    async fn run_process(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n        adapter: &AgentAdapter,\n        workspace: &Path,\n        prompt_file: &Path,\n    ) -> Result<ExecutionResult> {\n        // Create trace capture for this bead execution.\n        // Sanitizer is cloned (Arc clone — cheap) and applied before every disk write.\n        let trace_capture =\n            TraceCapture::new_with_sanitizer(bead_id, workspace, self.sanitizer.clone());\n\n        // Provision tsnet identity if enabled\n        let worker_id = self.telemetry.worker_id().to_string();\n        let tsnet_identity = if let Some(ref registry) = self.tsnet_registry {\n            match registry.provision_identity(&worker_id, bead_id).await {\n                Ok(identity) => Some(identity),\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        worker_id = %worker_id,\n                        bead_id = %bead_id.as_ref(),\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to provision tsnet identity, continuing without network identity\"\n                    );\n                    None\n                }\n            }\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        let model = adapter.model.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"default\");\n        let rendered = render_template(\n            &adapter.invoke_template,\n            workspace,\n            prompt_file,\n            bead_id,\n            model,\n        );\n\n        // Build environment variables for the child process\n        let mut child_env = adapter.environment.clone();\n\n        // Inject tsnet identity environment variables if provisioned\n        if let (Some(ref identity), Some(_)) = (&tsnet_identity, &self.tsnet_registry) {\n            inject_identity_env(identity, &self.tsnet_config, &mut child_env);\n        }\n\n        // Spawn the agent process with ETXTBSY retry handling.\n        // This wrapper retries with backoff if the kernel returns ETXTBSY (errno 26),\n        // which can occur when a binary has been written to disk and immediately executed.\n        let rendered_clone = rendered.clone();\n        let child_env_clone = child_env.clone();\n        let adapter_name_clone = adapter.name.clone();\n        let mut child = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_child(\n            || {\n                let rendered = rendered_clone.clone();\n                let child_env = child_env_clone.clone();\n                let adapter_name = adapter_name_clone.clone();\n                async move {\n                    // Safety: setpgid(0,0) is async-signal-safe and idempotent.\n                    unsafe {\n                        tokio::process::Command::new(\"bash\")\n                            .arg(\"-c\")\n                            .arg(&rendered)\n                            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n                            .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n                            .envs(&child_env)\n .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn agent: {}\", adapter.name))?;\n\n        let pid = child.id().unwrap_or(0);\n        tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.agent.pid\", pid);\n        let                     // try_send drops lines when the transform is\n                                // slower than the agent.\n                                let (tx, mut rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::channel::<String>(64);\n                                let transform_start = Instant::now();\n\n                                // Feeder task: forwards channel lines to\n                                // transform stdin.  Dropping the writer closes\n                                // stdin → transform receives EOF.  The handle\n                                // is kept (not fire-and-forget) so the caller\n                                // can confirm the feeder actually finished\n bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                            error: e.to_string(),\n                            exit_code: -1,\n                        });\n                        (None, None, None, None, (None, Some(hard)) => Some(hard),\n                    (None, None) => None,\n                };\n\n                select! {\n                    // Branch 1: child exited (natural or signaled)\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Helpers\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Compute the per-bead agent log path: `~/.needle/logs/<worker>-<bead_id>.agent.jsonl`.\n///\n/// Build a trace sanitizer from the workspace config.\n///\n/// Returns `None` if sanitization is disabled or if rule      // represent actual strand activity.\n                if should_record {\n                    strand_evaluations.push(StrandEvaluation {\n                        strand_name:                            .collect();\n                        let excluded_count = original_count.saturating_sub(filtered.len());\n\n                        // Record queue depth for the Pluck                          strand = %strand_name,\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"failed to emit strand evaluated telemetry\"\n             \"failed to emit strand evaluated telemetry\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                        restarts += 1;\n                  reason: reason.clone(),\n                })?;\n                Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable { reason })\n            }\n            Ok(other) => {\n                // RaceLost shouldn't happen with claim_auto, but handle it\n                tracing::warn!(?other, \"claim_auto returned unexpected result\");\n                Ok(other)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                let reason = format!(\"store error: {e}\");\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", &reason);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", &reason);\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                    bead_id: BeadId::from(\"(auto)\".to_string()),\n                    reason: reason.clone(),\n                })?;\n                Err(e)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute a deterministic lock file path for a workspace.\n///\n/// Uses a simple hash (not crypto) of the workspace path. All workers\n/// compute the same hash for the same workspace.\nfn workspace_lock_path(lock_dir: &Path, workspace: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n    let mut hasher = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();\n    workspace.hash(&mut hasher);\n    let hash = hasher.finish();\n    lock_dir.join(format!(\"needle-claim-{:016x}.lock\", hash))\n}\n\n/// Acquire an exclusive flock with a 10-second timeout.\n///\n/// Returns the locked file on success. The lock is released when the\n/// file is dropped (flock auto-releases on close).\npub async fn acquire_flock(lock_path: &Path) -> Result<std::fs::File> {\n    if let Some(parent) = lock_path.parent() {\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;\n    }\n\n    let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n        .create(true)\n        .truncate(false)\n        .write(true)\n        .open(lock_path)?;\n\n    let deadline = Instant::now() + FLOCK_TIMEOUT;\n    loop {\n        match file.try_lock_exclusive() {\n            Ok(()) => return Ok(file),\n            Err(ref e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {\n                if Instant::now() >= deadline {\n                    return Err(anyhow!(\n                        \"flock timeout after {}s on {}\",\n                        FLOCK_TIMEOUT.as_secs(),\n                        lock_path.display()\n                    ));\n                }\n                tokio::time::sleep(FLOCK_POLL_INTERVAL).await;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use { .. }\n            | EventKind::MendBeadReleaseFailed { .. }\n            | EventKind::MendDependencyCleanupFailed { .. }\n            | EventKind::MendLockRemoveFailed { .. }\n            |    | EventKind::UpgradeDetected { .. }\n            | EventKind::UpgradeCompleted { .. }\n            | EventKind::RollbackCompleted { .. }\n            | EventKind::CanaryStarted { .. }\n EventKind::OtlpShutdownTimeout { .. }\n            | EventKind::DriftDetectionStarted { .. }\n            | EventKind::DriftDetectionCompleted { .. }\n            | EventKind::DriftDetectionSkipped { .. }\n            | EventKind::DriftReportWritten { .. }\n            | EventKind::DecisionDetectionStarted { .. }\n            | EventKind::DecisionDetectionCompleted { .. }\n            |       EventKind::UpgradeCheckCompleted { .. } => None,\n            EventKind::UpgradeCheckFailed { .. } => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Serialize event-specific payload to a JSON value.\n    pub fn to_data(&self) -> serde_json::Value {\n        match self {\n            EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStarted {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStopped {\n                reason,\n                beads_processed,\n                uptime_secs,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"reason\": reason,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                    \"uptime_secs\": uptime_secs,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerErrored {\n                error_type,\n                error_message,\n                beads_processed,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"error_type\": error_type,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerExhausted {\n                cycle_count,\n                last_strand,\n                waterfall_restarts,\n                restart_triggers,\n                strand_evaluations,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"cycle_count\": cycle_count,\n                    \"last_strand_evaluated\": last_strand,\n                    \"waterfall_restarts\": waterfall_restarts,\n                    \"restart_triggers\": restart_triggers,\n                    \"strand_evaluations\": strand_evaluations,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerIdle { backoff_seconds } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"backoff_seconds\": backoff_seconds })\n            }\n            EventKind::StateTransition { from, to } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"from\": format!(\"{from}\"), \"to\": format!(\"{to}\") })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepStarted { step } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepCompleted { step, duration_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step, \"duration_ms\": duration_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerBootTimeout { elapsed_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"elapsed_ms\": elapsed_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerLaunchDeferred {\n                deferred_count,\n                total_wait_secs,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"deferred_count\": deferred_count,\n                    \"total_wait_secs\": total_wait_secs,\n                    \"reason\": reason\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                strand_name,\n                result,\n                duration_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"result\": result,\n                    \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandSkipped {\n                strand_name,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"strand_name\": strand_name, \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadStoreError {\n                strand_name,\n                operation,\n                error_message,\n                stderr,\n                exit_code,\n                workspace,\n            } => {\n                let mut data = serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"operation\": operation,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"stderr\": stderr,\n                    \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n                });\n                if let Some(ws) = workspace {\n                    if let Some(obj) = data.as_object_mut() {\n                        obj.insert(\"workspace\".to_string(), serde_json::json!(ws));\n                    }\n                }\n                data\n            }\n            EventKind::QueueEmpty => serde_json::json!({}),\n            EventKind::PluckStarvationDetected {\n                workspace,\n                open_count,\n                excluded_count,\n                candidate_exclusion_reasons,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"workspace\": workspace,\n                    \"open_count\": open_count,\n                    \"excluded_count\": excluded_count,\n                    \"candidate_exclusion_reasons\": candidate_exclusion_reasons,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimAttempt { bead_id, attempt } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"attempt\": attempt })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimSuccess {\n                bead_id,\n                priority,\n                strand,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"priority\": priority,\n                    \"strand\": strand,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimRaceLost { bead_id } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref() })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimRaceLostSkipped {\n                consecutive_losses,\n                threshold,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"consecutive_losses\": consecutive_losses,\n                    \"threshold\": threshold,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::ClaimFailed { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadReleased { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadCompleted {\n                bead_id,\n                duration_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"duration_ms\": duration_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadOrphaned { bead_id } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref() })\n            }\n            EventKind::DispatchStarted {\n                bead_id,\n                agent,\n                prompt_len,\n                template_name,\n                template_version,\n                prompt_hash,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"agent\": agent,\n                    \"prompt_len\": prompt_len,\n                    \"template_name\": template_name,\n                    \"template_version\": template_version,\n                    \"prompt_hash\": format!(\"sha256:{prompt_hash}\"),\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::DispatchCompleted {\n                bead_id,\n                   \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n                    \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n                    \"agent\": agent,\n                    \"model\": model,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::RoutingDecision {\n                bead_id,\n                model,\n                matched_rule,\n                chosen_adapter,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"model\": model,\n                    \"matched_rule\": matched_rule,\n                    \"chosen_adapter\": chosen_adapter,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::RoutingFailed {\n                bead_id,\n                model,\n                rules_tried,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"model\": model,\n                    \"rules_tried\": rules_tried,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::AgentTimeout { bead_id, reason } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n EventKind::BuildHeartbeat {\n                bead_id,\n                elapsed_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"elapsed_ms\": elapsed_ms,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::OutcomeClassified {\n                bead_id,\n                outcome,\n                exit_code,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"outcome\": outcome,\n                    \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::OutcomeHandled {\n                bead_id,\n                outcome,\n                action,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n                    \"outcome\": outcome,\n                    \"action\": action,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                bead_id,\n                outcome,\n                operation,\n                error,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n            }\n            EventKind::HeartbeatEmitted { bead_id, state } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref().map(|b| b.as_ref()),\n                    \"state\": state,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StuckDetected { bead_id, age_secs } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(), \"age_secs\": age_secs })\n            }\n            EventKind::StuckReleased {\n                bead_id,\n                peer_worker,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ peer_count,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"db_healthy\": db_healthy,\n                    \"disk_free_mb\": disk_free_mb,\n                    \"peer_count\": peer_count,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::FleetCpuSaturated {\n                load_average,\n                threshold,\n                core_count,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"load_average\": load_average,\n                    \"threshold\": threshold,\n                    \"core_count\": core_count,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::FleetMemoryLow {\n                free_mb,\n                threshold_mb,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"free_mb\": free_mb,\n                    \"threshold_mb\": threshold_mb,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::MendOrphanedLockRemoved {\n                lock_path,\n                age_secs,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"lock_path\": lock_path, \"age_secs\": age_secs })\n            }\n            EventKind::MendDependencyCleaned {\n                bead_id,\n                blocker_id,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"bead_id\": bead_id.as_ref(),\n               \"model\": model,\n                    \"tokens_in\": tokens_in,\n                    \"tokens_out\": tokens_out,\n                    \"estimated_cost_usd\": estimated_cost_usd,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::BudgetWarning {\n                daily_cost,\n                threshold,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n            EventKind::RateLimitWait {\n                provider,\n                model,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n to add a new sink — register an instance in the\n/// `TelemetryBus` and events fan out automatically, with no special-casing.\npub trait Sink: Send + Sync {\n    /// Accept a single event. Must not block indefinitely.\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Flush any buffered state before shutdown.\n    ///\n    /// Implementations should respect `deadline`: if flushing cannot complete\n    /// within the duration, return an error rather than blocking indefinitely.\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Blanket impl for Arc-wrapped sinks.\n/// This enables Arc<Sink> to be used wherever Sink is required.\nimpl<T: Sink + ?Sized> Sink for Arc<T> {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        self.as_ref().accept(event)\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        self.as_ref().flush(deadline)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── StdoutSink ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Human-readable, color-coded telemetry sink for interactive monitoring.\n///\n/// Format: `HH:MM:SS [worker] EVENT detail`\npub struct StdoutSink {\n    format: StdoutFormat,\n    use_color: bool,\n}\n\nimpl StdoutSink {\n    /// Create a new stdout sink from config.\n    pub fn new(config: &StdoutSinkConfig) -> Self {\n        let use_color = match config.color {\n            ColorMode::Always => true,\n            ColorMode::Never => false,\n            ColorMode::Auto => atty_stdout(),\n        };\n        StdoutSink {\n            format: config.format,\n            use_color,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Format a single event as a human-readable line.\n    pub fn format_event(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> String {\n        let time = event.timestamp.format(\"%H:%M:%S\");\n        let worker = &event.worker_id;\n        let etype = &event.event_type;\n\n        // Build the summary portion based on event type.\n        let summary = self.event_summary(event);\n\n        match self.format {\n            StdoutFormat::Minimal => {\n                let line = format!(\"{time} [{worker}] {etype}\");\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n            StdoutFormat::Normal => {\n                let bead_part = event\n                    .bead_id\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map(|b| format!(\" {}\", b.as_ref()))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let summary_part = if summary.is_empty() {\n                    String::new()\n                } else {\n                    format!(\" ({summary})\")\n                };\n                let line = format!(\n                    \"{time} [{worker}] {}{bead_part}{summary_part}\",\n                    Self::short_type(etype)\n                );\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n            StdoutFormat::Verbose => {\n                let bead_part = event\n                    .bead_id\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map(|b| format!(\" {}\", b.as_ref()))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let data_part = if event.data.is_object()\n                    && event.data.as_object().map_or(true, |m| m.is_empty())\n                {\n                    String::new()\n                } else {\n                    format!(\" {}\", event.data)\n                };\n                let dur = event\n                    .duration_ms\n                    .map(|d| format!(\" {}ms\", d))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let line = format!(\n                    \"{time} [{worker}] {}{bead_part}{dur}{data_part}\",\n                    Self::short_type(etype)\n                );\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Shorten the dotted event type to an uppercase action word.\n    fn short_type(event_type: &str) -> &str {\n        match event_type {\n            \"worker.started\" => \"STARTED\",\n            \"worker.stopped\" => \"STOPPED\",\n            \"worker.errored\" => \"ERROR\",\n            \"worker.exhausted\" => \"EXHAUSTED\",\n            \"worker.idle\" => \"IDLE\",\n            \"worker.state_transition\" => \"STATE\",\n            \"worker.queue_empty\" => \"QUEUE_EMPTY\",\n            \"strand.evaluated\" => \"STRAND\",\n            \"strand.skipped\" => \"STRAND_SKIP\",\n            \"bead.claim.attempted\" => \"CLAIMING\",\n            \"bead.claim.succeeded\" => \"CLAIMED\",\n            \"bead.claim.race_lost\" => \"RACE_LOST\",\n            \"bead.claim.race_lost_skipped\" => \"RACE_LOST_SKIP\",\n            \"bead.claim.failed\" => \"CLAIM_FAIL\",\n            \"bead.released\" => \"RELEASED\",\n            \"bead.completed\" => \"COMPLETED\",\n            \"bead.orphaned\" => \"ORPHANED\",\n            \"agent.dispatched\" => \"DISPATCHED\",\n            \"agent.completed\" => \"AGENT_DONE\",\n            \"outcome.classified\" => \"OUTCOME\",\n            \"outcome.handled\" => \"HANDLED\",\n            \"heartbeat.emitted\" => \"HEARTBEAT\",\n            \"peer.stale\" => \"PEER_STALE\",\n            \"peer.crashed\" => \"PEER_CRASHED\",\n            \"health.check\" => \"HEALTH\",\n            \"effort.recorded\" => \"EFFORT\",\n            \"budget.warning\" => \"BUDGET_WARN\",\n            \"budget.stop\" => \"BUDGET_STOP\",\n            \"rate_limit.wait\" => \"RATE_WAIT\",\n            \"rate_limit.allowed\" => \"RATE_OK\",\n            \"bead.mitosis.evaluated\" => \"MITOSIS_EVAL\",\n            \"bead.mitosis.split\" => \"MITOSIS\",\n            \"bead.mitosis.skipped\" => \"MITOSIS_SKIP\",\n            \"mend.orphaned_lock_removed\" => \"MEND_LOCK\",\n            \"mend.dependency_cleaned\" => \"MEND_DEP\",\n            \"mend.db_repaired\" => \"MEND_REPAIR\",\n            \"mend.db_rebuilt\" => \"MEND_REBUILD\",\n            \"mend.cycle_summary\" => \"MEND_DONE\",\n            \"telemetry.sink_error\" => \"SINK_ERR\",\n            other => other,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Produce a brief summary from the event data.\n    fn event_summary(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> String {\n        let d = &event.data;\n        match event.event_type.as_str() {\n            \"bead.claim.succeeded\" => String::new(),\n            \"agent.dispatched\" => d[\"agent\"]\n                .as_str()\n                .map(|a| format!(\"agent={a}\"))\n                .unwrap_or_default(),\n            \"agent.completed\" => {\n                let exit = d[\"exit_code\"].as_i64().unwrap_or(-1);\n                let dur = d[\"duration_ms\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"exit={exit}, {}\", format_duration_ms(dur))\n            }\n            \"outcome.classified\" => d[\"outcome\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string(),\n            \"outcome.handled\" => {\n                let outcome = d[\"outcome\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                let action = d[\"action\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                format!(\"{outcome} → {action}\")\n            }\n            \"effort.recorded\" => {\n                let agent = d[\"agent_name\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                let cost = d[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64();\n                let dur = d[\"elapsed_ms\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                match cost {\n                    Some(c) => format!(\"{agent}, {}, ${c:.4}\", format_duration_ms(dur)),\n                    None => format!(\"{agent}, {}\", format_duration_ms(dur)),\n                }\n            }\n            \"worker.stopped\" => {\n                let reason = d[\"reason\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                let beads = d[\"beads_processed\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"{reason}, {beads} beads\")\n            }\n            \"worker.errored\" => d[\"error_message\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string(),\n            \"worker.idle\" => {\n                let secs = d[\"backoff_seconds\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"backoff {secs}s\")\n            }\n            \"bead.mitosis.split\" => {\n                let created = d[\"children_created\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"{created} children\")\n            }\n            \"budget.warning\" | \"budget.stop\" => {\n                let cost = d[\"daily_cost\"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);\n                let thresh = d[\"threshold\"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);\n                format!(\"${cost:.2}/${thresh:.2}\")\n            }\n            _ => String::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Wrap text in ANSI color based on event type category.\n    fn colorize(&self, event_type: &str, text: &str) -> String {\n        let code = match event_type {\n            t if t.starts_with(\"worker.errored\") || t.starts_with(\"budget.stop\") => \"\\x1b[31m\", // red\n            t if t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.succeeded\") || t == \"bead.completed\" => \"\\x1b[32m\", // green\n            t if t.starts_with(\"agent.\") || t.starts_with(\"outcome.\") => \"\\x1b[36m\", // cyan\n            t if t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.race_lost\")\n                || t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.race_lost_skipped\")\n                || t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.failed\")\n                || t == \"bead.released\"\n                || t == \"bead.orphaned\" =>\n            {\n                \"\\x1b[33m\"\n            } // yellow\n            t if t.starts_with(\"budget.warning\") || t.starts_with(\"rate_limit\") => \"\\x1b[33m\", // yellow\n            t if t.starts_with(\"mend.\") || t.starts_with(\"peer.\") => \"\\x1b[35m\", // magenta\n            t if t.starts_with(\"heartbeat\") || t.starts_with(\"health\") => \"\\x1b[90m\", // dim\n            _ => \"\\x1b[0m\",                                                      // reset / default\n        };\n        format!(\"{code}{text}\\x1b[0m\")\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for StdoutSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        let line = self.format_event(event);\n        println!(\"{line}\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, _deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        std::io::stdout().flush()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if stdout is a terminal (for auto color detection).\nfn atty_stdout() -> bool {\n    unsafe { libc_isatty(1) != 0 }\n}\n\nextern \"C\" {\n    #[link_name = \"isatty\"]\n    fn libc_isatty(fd: i32) -> i32;\n}\n\n/// Public wrapper for formatting milliseconds as human-readable duration.\npub fn format_duration_ms_public(ms: u64) -> String {\n    format_duration_ms(ms)\n}\n\n/// Format milliseconds as human-readable duration.\nfn format_duration_ms(ms: u64) -> String {\n    if ms < 1000 {\n        format!(\"{ms}ms\")\n    } else if ms < 60_000 {\n        format!(\"{:.1}s\", ms as f64 / 1000.0)\n    } else {\n        let mins = ms / 60_000;\n        let secs = (ms % 60_000) / 1000;\n        format!(\"{mins}m{secs}s\")\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Session ID generation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Generate an 8-hex-char session ID.\n///\n/// Uses `/dev/urandom` when available, falls back to PID XOR timestamp.\npub fn generate_session_id() -> String {\n    // Try /dev/urandom (Linux/macOS)\n    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::File::open(\"/dev/urandom\") {\n        use std::io::Read;\n        let mut buf = [0u8; 4];\n        if f.read_exact(&mut buf).is_ok() {\n            return format!(\"{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}\", buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3]);\n        }\n    }\n    // Fallback: PID XOR nanosecond timestamp\n    let pid = std::process::id();\n    let ts = Utc::now().timestamp_millis() as u64;\n    let hash = pid as u64 ^ ts;\n    format!(\"{:08x}\", hash & 0xffff_ffff)\n}\n\n// ─── Trace context helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Returns `(trace_id_hex, span_id_hex)` from the current OTel span context,\n/// or `(None, None)` when not inside a valid span.\n#[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\nfn current_trace_ids() -> (Option<String>, Option<String>) {\n    use opentelemetry::trace::TraceContextExt;\n    let ctx = opentelemetry::Context::current();\n    let binding = ctx.span();\n    let span_ctx = binding.span_context();\n    if span_ctx.is_valid() {\n        (\n            Some(hex::encode(span_ctx.trace_id().to_bytes())),\n            Some(hex::encode(span_ctx.span_id().to_bytes())),\n        )\n    } else {\n        (None, None)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\nfn current_trace_ids() -> (Option<String>, Option<String>) {\n    (None, None)\n}\n\n// ─── HookSink ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A compiled hook: a pre-compiled regex filter + dispatch target(s).\nstruct CompiledHook {\n    filter: regex::Regex,\n    /// Shell command (empty = disabled).\n    command: String,\n    /// Webhook URL (None = disabled).\n    url: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Dispatches matching telemetry events to external commands and/or URLs.\n///\n/// Each hook has a glob pattern matched against `event_type`. When an event\n/// matches, the event JSON is piped to `command`'s stdin and/or HTTP-POSTed\n/// to `url`. Execution is fire-and-forget — failed hooks emit `SinkError`\n/// events to the file sink but never block the worker or recurse into hooks.\npub struct HookSink {\n    hooks: Vec<CompiledHook>,\n}\n\nimpl HookSink {\n    /// Compile hook configs into a `HookSink`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if any `event_filter` is an invalid glob pattern.\n    pub fn new(configs: &[crate::config::HookConfig]) -> Result<Self> {\n        let mut hooks = Vec::with_capacity(configs.len());\n        for cfg in configs {\n            let filter = glob_to_regex(&cfg.event_filter)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid hook filter: {}\", cfg.event_filter))?;\n            hooks.push(CompiledHook {\n                filter,\n                command: cfg.command.clone(),\n                url: cfg.url.clone(),\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(HookSink { hooks })\n    }\n\n    /// Check whether any hooks are configured.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.hooks.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Dispatch an event to all matching hooks (fire-and-forget).\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of `SinkError` events for hooks that failed, so the\n    /// caller can write them to the file sink without recursion.\n    pub fn dispatch(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Vec<TelemetryEvent> {\n        // Never dispatch SinkError events to hooks — prevents recursion.\n        if event.event_type == \"telemetry.sink_error\" {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n\n        let json = match serde_json::to_string(event) {\n            Ok(j) => j,\n            Err(_) => return Vec::new(),\n        };\n\n        let mut failures = Vec::new();\n        for hook in &self.hooks {\n            if !hook.filter.is_match(&event.event_type) {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Dispatch to command if configured.\n            if !hook.command.is_empty() {\n                match Self::run_hook(&hook.command, &json) {\n                    Ok(()) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        failures.push(TelemetryEvent {\n                            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n                            event_type: \"telemetry.sink_error\".to_string(),\n                            worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                            session_id: event.session_id.clone(),\n                            sequence: 0, // sequence is set by the emitter, not here\n                            bead_id: None,\n                            workspace: None,\n                            data: serde_json::json!({\n                                \"hook_command\": hook.command,\n                                \"event_filter\": hook.filter.as_str(),\n                                \"original_event_type\": event.event_type,\n                                \"error\": e.to_string(),\n                            }),\n                            duration_ms: None,\n                            trace_id: None,\n                            span_id: None,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Dispatch to URL if configured.\n            if let Some(ref url) = hook.url {\n                match Self::post_url(url, &json) {\n                    Ok(()) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        failures.push(TelemetryEvent {\n                            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n                            event_type: \"telemetry.sink_error\".to_string(),\n                            worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                            session_id: event.session_id.clone(),\n                            sequence: 0,\n                            bead_id: None,\n                            workspace: None,\n                            data: serde_json::json!({\n                                \"hook_url\": url,\n                                \"event_filter\": hook.filter.as_str(),\n                                \"original_event_type\": event.event_type,\n                                \"error\": e.to_string(),\n                            }),\n                            duration_ms: None,\n                            trace_id: None,\n                            span_id: None,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        failures\n    }\n\n    /// Execute a single hook command, piping JSON to its stdin.\n    ///\n    /// Spawns `sh -c <command>` with the event JSON on stdin, waits for\n    /// completion, and returns an error if the command exits non-zero.\n    /// This runs inside the background writer task so blocking is acceptable.\n    fn run_hook(command: &str, json: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        use std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n\n        let mut child = Command::new(\"sh\")\n            .arg(\"-c\")\n            .arg(command)\n            .stdin(Stdio::piped())\n            .stdout(Stdio::null())\n            .stderr(Stdio::null())\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn hook: {command}\"))?;\n\n        if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {\n            // Best-effort write; ignore broken pipe if child exits early.\n            let _ = stdin.write_all(json.as_bytes());\n        }\n\n        // Wait for the child and check exit status.\n        let status = child\n            .wait()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to wait for hook: {command}\"))?;\n\n        if !status.success() {\n            anyhow::bail!(\n                \"hook exited with status {}: {command}\",\n                status.code().unwrap_or(-1)\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// HTTP POST the event JSON to a webhook URL.\n    ///\n    /// Sets `Content-Type: application/json` and applies a 10-second timeout.\n    /// Returns an error if the request fails or the server returns a non-2xx\n    /// status. This runs inside the background writer task so blocking is\n    /// acceptable.\n    fn post_url(url: &str, json: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        ureq::post(url)\n            .set(\"Content-Type\", \"application/json\")\n            .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10))\n            .send_string(json)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"webhook POST to {url} failed: {e}\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for HookSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        let failures = self.dispatch(event);\n        for fail in &failures {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                hook_error = %fail.data,\n                original_event = %event.event_type,\n                \"telemetry hook dispatch failed\"\n            );\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, _deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        // hooks run synchronously in accept(); nothing to drain\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Telemetry emitter ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Non-blocking telemetry emitter.\n///\n/// Cloning a `Telemetry` handle is cheap — it shares the same background\n/// writer and sequence counter.\n///\n/// The writer task must be started by calling `start()` from within a tokio\n/// runtime context. This is typically done at the beginning of `Worker::run()`.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Telemetry {\n    worker_id: WorkerId,\n    session_id: String,\n    sequence: Arc<AtomicU64>,\n    /// Workspace of the most recently claimed bead, shared by all telemetry handles.\n    current_workspace: Arc<std::sync::RwLock<Option<PathBuf>>>,\n    /// Wrapped in Arc<Mutex<Option<...>>> so that `shutdown()` can drop the\n    /// sender explicitly (closing the channel) even while clones still exist.\n    sender: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<mpsc::UnboundedSender<WriterMessage>>>>,\n    /// Pending writer state that needs to be spawned in an async context.\n    /// This is `Some` until `start()` is called.\n    pending_writer: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<PendingWriter>>>,\n    /// JoinHandle for the background writer thread, set by `start()`.\n    /// Uses std::thread::JoinHandle (not tokio::task::JoinHandle) because the\n    /// writer runs in its own dedicated thread with its own tokio runtime,\n    /// ensuring it can process messages before the main runtime's block_on().\n    writer_handle: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>>>,\n    /// OTLP sink shutdown handle (feature-gated).\n    /// Stored separately so we can call its async shutdown method.\n    otlp_shutdown: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<OtlpShutdown>>>,\n}\n\n/// Worker identity used to populate OTLP resource attributes.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct TelemetryIdentity {\n    /// The configured worker agent or harness name.\n    pub agent: Option<String>,\n    /// The resolved model identifier, when the adapter declares one.\n    pub model: Option<String>,\n    /// The worker's workspace. OTLP sinks reduce this to its basename before export.\n    pub workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n}\n\n/// Internal message type for the writer task.\n#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]\nenum WriterMessage {\n    Event(TelemetryEvent),\n    Flush(tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<()>),\n}\n\n/// Holds the receiver and sinks until they can be spawned in an async context.\nstruct PendingWriter {\n    receiver: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<WriterMessage>,\n    sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>>,\n}\n\n/// Holds an OTLP sink for async shutdown (feature-gated).\nenum OtlpShutdown {\n    #[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n    Sink(std::sync::Arc<crate::telemetry::OtlpSink>),\n    #[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\n    None,\n}\n\nimpl OtlpShutdown {\n    /// Shutdown the OTLP sink gracefully.\n    ///\n    /// This drains all batched exports before returning.\n    #[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n    async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<()> {\n        match self {\n            OtlpShutdown::Sink(sink) => {\n                // We need to extract the OtlpSink from Arc to call shutdown\n                // Try to unwrap the Arc - if there are other references, we'll force_flush instead\n                match std::sync::Arc::try_unwrap(sink) {\n                    Ok(otlp) => otlp.shutdown().await,\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\"Cannot shutdown OTLP sink: Arc has multiple references\");\n                        Ok(())\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// No-op shutdown when OTLP feature is disabled.\n    #[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\n    async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<()> {\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Telemetry {\n    fn new_workspace_cell() -> Arc<std::sync::RwLock<Option<PathBuf>>> {\n        Arc::new(std::sync::RwLock::new(None))\n    }\n\n    /// Create a telemetry emitter that writes to a `FileSink`.\n    ///\n    /// Does not spawn any async tasks. Call [`start()`](Self::start) from\n    /// within a tokio runtime context before emitting events.\n    ///\n    /// Writes `worker.booting` directly to the file before returning, so even\n    /// if the writer thread fails to start, we have a trace in the JSONL log.\n    pub fn new(worker_id: WorkerId) -> Self {\n        let session_id = generate_session_id();\n        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();\n\n        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();\n        match FileSink::new(&worker_id, &session_id) {\n            Ok(s) => {\n                // Write boot event directly to file BEFORE spawning writer thread.\n                // Uses a 5-second timeout to prevent indefinite blocking on hung filesystems.\n                // This ensures we have a trace even if the writer thread fails to start.\n                let version = env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\");\n                if let Err(e) = s.write_boot_event_direct(&worker_id, &session_id, version) {\n                    // Check if this is a timeout error (filesystem may be hung)\n                    let error_msg = e.to_string();\n                    if error_msg.contains(\"timed out\")\n                        || error_msg.contains(\"filesystem may be hung\")\n                    {\n                        eprintln!(\n                            \"NEEDLE WARNING: boot event write timed out after 5s - filesystem may be hung or very slow\"\n                        );\n                        eprintln!(\"  Continuing without boot event in log file. Worker will still function.\");\n                        eprintln!(\n                            \"  Check: disk space, NFS mounts, filesystem latency, I/O errors\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to write boot event directly to file\");\n                }\n                sinks.push(Box::new(s));\n            }\n            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to create telemetry file sink\"),\n        }\n\n        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));\n        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };\n\n        Telemetry {\n            worker_id,\n            session_id,\n            sequence,\n            current_workspace: Self::new_workspace_cell(),\n            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),\n            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),\n            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a telemetry emitter with both file and stdout sinks.\n    ///\n    /// Does not spawn any async tasks. Otherwise          → [`new`](Self::new) (file sink only)\n    pub fn from_config(worker_id: WorkerId, config: &TelemetryConfig) -> Result<Self> {\n        Self::from_config_with_identity(worker_id, config, &TelemetryIdentity::default())\n    }\n\n    /// Create a telemetry emitter from configuration with worker identity metadata.\n    ///\n    /// This is the construction path used by a running worker.   let session_id = generate_session_id();\n        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();\n\n        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();\n        let mut otlp_shutdown =
